q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of HDPE pipe per kg or per metre?
title: HDPE pipe carbon footprint per kg
short: Multiply the resin per metre of pipe by your polymer supplier's per-kg figure. Add the extrusion line's electricity, cooling, printing and coiling, divide plant energy by kg passed, and convert to per metre using the pipe's weight per metre.

ul: PE 80 or PE 100 resin by weight; resin is usually most of the total.
Black masterbatch and any regrind used.
End caps, coil straps and labels.
Extruder barrel heaters and screw drive.
Vacuum sizing tank, cooling baths and chiller.

p: Give both, with the pipe's outside diameter and pressure class, since weight per metre rises sharply with both.

example.title: Worked example: HDPE pipe plant per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 127,800 / 400,000 = 0.320 kg CO2 per kg
Add PE resin and masterbatch for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
